name: blueprint/task-triage
description: Turn an unstructured inbox into a task board: rh_text_classify sorts items into your labels, rh_text_extract pulls the structured fields, rh_task_create boards them, rh_task_next drives the work loop, and a failed task records what went wrong instead of going quiet.
use_cases: extract a due date from text
what should I work on now
a task that failed must say why
ingredients: rh_task_create / rh_task_list / rh_task_next / rh_task_update / rh_task_delete (typed domain, open -> done/failed)
rh_text_classify / rh_text_extract / rh_text_summarise (ctx.llm, one call per verb)
rh_store for the inbox items before they are boarded
recipe: capture items under inbox: -> rh_text_classify into your label set -> rh_text_extract the structured fields (due, amount, owner) -> rh_task_create one task per item -> work loop: rh_task_next returns the oldest open task -> finish with rh_task_update state done, or failed with a result saying what was tried and what broke -> weekly: rh_text_summarise over done tasks for the report
result_kind: task board (open -> done/failed) plus one summary per review

invoke_contract.extract: { text, schema } -> one object conforming to the schema

config_variants.model: text family config provider/model, default harness default

cost_hint: one model call per verb (classify/extract/summarise); tasks and store are free
pitfalls: classify returns a label VERBATIM from your set plus 0-1 confidence - a label outside the set is an error, not a guess
extract takes a JSON Schema; parse failures surface as a clean error, never raw prose
rh_task_next is the oldest open task - the work loop is deterministic, not a choice
a task that cannot run is still recorded: update it failed with a result, never delete the evidence
each verb is one contained model call - one failure does not take down the others
local_limits: the LLM is the harness default unless the text family config says otherwise
cloud_limits: same text family on the user's own Cloudflare account if the model provider is theirs
